title: [Bugs] Resource Leak in AMF when Unexpected InitialUEMessage Service Request Received
body:
## Describe the bug
The AMF experiences a resource leak after logging "No Security Context : SUPI[]" when receiving an InitialUEMessage Service Request at an unexpected timing.

## To Reproduce
If the following sequence occurs for the same 5G-S-TMSI, the AmfUe is not released, leading to a resource leak:

  1.   UE Context Release Request (NG-RAN node initiated) (gNB -> AMF)
  2.   UEContextReleaseCommand (AMF -> gNB)
  3.   InitialUEMessage Service Request (gNB -> AMF)
  3.1. AMF attaches new ranUe
  4.   UEContextReleaseComplete (gNB -> AMF)

## Expected behavior
AMF should release old resources and then switch to new resources:

  1.   UE Context Release Request (NG-RAN node initiated)(gNB -> AMF)
  2.   UEContextReleaseCommand(AMF -> gNB)
  3.   InitialUEMessage Service Request(gNB -> AMF)
  3.1 AMF should detach old ranUe
  3.2 AMF should attach new ranUe

## Walkthrough
The resource leak occurs when the else case in the HandleNAS function is executed. It seems that the leak happens because the old AmfUe is not released, and a new AmfUe ("") is used instead.

Note1.
  The evaluation result of this if statement is the behavior of evaluating if(true && false).
>         if ranUe.HoldingAmfUe != nil && !ranUe.HoldingAmfUe.CmConnect(ranUe.Ran.AnType) { 　
        
```
func HandleNAS(ranUe *amf_context.RanUe, procedureCode int64, nasPdu []byte, initialMessage bool) {
    ...
    if ranUe.AmfUe == nil {
        // Only the New created RanUE will have no AmfUe in it
        if ranUe.HoldingAmfUe != nil && !ranUe.HoldingAmfUe.CmConnect(ranUe.Ran.AnType) { 　
            // If the UE is CM-IDLE, there is no RanUE in AmfUe, so here we attach new RanUe to AmfUe.
            gmm_common.AttachRanUeToAmfUeAndReleaseOldIfAny(ranUe.HoldingAmfUe, ranUe)
            ranUe.HoldingAmfUe = nil
        } else { //
            // Assume we have an existing UE context in CM-CONNECTED state. (RanUe <-> AmfUe)
            // We will release it if the new UE context has a valid security context(Authenticated) in line 50.
            ranUe.AmfUe = amfSelf.NewAmfUe(“”)
            gmm_common.AttachRanUeToAmfUeAndReleaseOldIfAny(ranUe.AmfUe, ranUe)
        }
    }
    ...
}
```

Note2.
If you pass NewAmfUe("") as the first argument to the AttachRanUeToAmfUeAndReleaseOldIfAny function,
the evaluation result of if will be false, which may result in a resource leak.

```
func AttachRanUeToAmfUeAndReleaseOldIfAny(amfUe *context.AmfUe, ranUe *context.RanUe) {
  if oldRanUe := amfUe.RanUe[ranUe.Ran.AnType]; oldRanUe != nil {
    oldRanUe.Log.Infof("Implicit Deregistration - RanUeNgapID[%d]", oldRanUe.RanUeNgapId)
    oldRanUe.DetachAmfUe()
    if amfUe.T3550 != nil {
      amfUe.State[ranUe.Ran.AnType].Set(context.Registered)
    }
    StopAll5GSMMTimers(amfUe)
    causeGroup := ngapType.CausePresentRadioNetwork
    causeValue := ngapType.CauseRadioNetworkPresentReleaseDueToNgranGeneratedReason
    ngap_message.SendUEContextReleaseCommand(oldRanUe, context.UeContextReleaseUeContext, causeGroup, causeValue)
  }
  amfUe.AttachRanUe(ranUe)
}
```

## Bug fix
If changing the arguments is acceptable, the following fix is ​​suggested:
```
func AttachRanUeToAmfUeAndReleaseOldIfAny(ranUe *context.RanUe) {

  if ranUe.amfUe != nil && oldRanUe := ranUe.amfUe.RanUe[ranUe.Ran.AnType]; oldRanUe != nil {
    amfUe := ranUe.amfUe
   
    oldRanUe.Log.Infof("Implicit Deregistration - RanUeNgapID[%d]", oldRanUe.RanUeNgapId)
    oldRanUe.DetachAmfUe()
    if amfUe.T3550 != nil {
      amfUe.State[ranUe.Ran.AnType].Set(context.Registered)
    }
    StopAll5GSMMTimers(amfUe)
    causeGroup := ngapType.CausePresentRadioNetwork
    causeValue := ngapType.CauseRadioNetworkPresentReleaseDueToNgranGeneratedReason
    ngap_message.SendUEContextReleaseCommand(oldRanUe, context.UeContextReleaseUeContext, causeGroup, causeValue)
   
  }
 
  ranUe.amfUe = amfSelf.NewAmfUe("")
  ranUe.amfUe.AttachRanUe(ranUe)
}
```

## Additional Context
This issue may be related to the changes introduced in the following fix: https://github.com/free5gc/free5gc/issues/580


## Environment
free5GC Version: v3.4.3
OS: Ubuntu 20.04.6 LTS
Kernel Version: 5.4.0-125-generic
Go Version: Ubuntu go1.21.8 linux/amd64
